opening_message:
Ticket 1: Matthew Mejia (employee ID E034) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E034.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Matthew Mejia (E034) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Payroll. As full-time employee, max is write (admin requires owning role; Analyst does not own Payroll). Requested level equals maximum, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E034 (Matthew Mejia) is a contractor with basic security training (prior note claiming full-time conflicts). Contractors max is read; write requires advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read for Payroll.
reason: The Security agent's note (looked up in their database) states E034 is a contractor with basic security training, and explicitly flags that the prior HR note claiming full-time conflicts with the Security DB record. Per policy, contractors max out at read unless they have advanced security training; basic training does not permit write. Therefore the requested write exceeds the maximum of read, so I grant read for Payroll.
